title: parseWhen reads a date with a month name in the server's time zone, so on a UTC server it is 5 h 30 min late
what_happens: The test 'records finds the repeated cards on a page, skipping the menu' failed in all 10 UTC runs and in none of the 10 IST runs. On a UTC machine parseWhen('02 Oct 2026') gives 2026-10-02T00:00Z, which is 05:30 in Chennai. The saved test also shows '02 Oct 2026 23:30' moving to the next Chennai day. This is a real product bug, not a test problem. The owner's laptop is in India, so it cannot be seen there. railway.json and package.json set no TZ, and DEPLOYMENT.md describes a Railway deployment; a server not set to India time would have this bug.
what_should_happen: A date with no time zone is Chennai time on any server, as the comment at sourcemap.ts:352 says.
repro: From chennai-grievance-portal-main: TZ=UTC npx vitest run src/lib/collector/sourcemap.test.ts (fails; passes with TZ=Asia/Kolkata). Saved as it.fails: npx vitest run --config vitest.qa4.config.ts tests/qa/pass4/flaky-parsewhen-tz.test.ts
root_cause_guess: src/lib/collector/sourcemap.ts:355 `new Date(s)` takes the string first and reads it in the machine's zone. The Chennai-time branch at lines 357-360 is reached only by forms new Date cannot read. The result goes into each item's published time at sourcemap.ts:374.
class: time zone: date read in the server's zone

title: 'recognises contact phrasing' ran out of its 15 s limit under load
what_happens: Failed in 1 of 20 runs (run 20, Asia/Kolkata, the slowest run at 118 s, while another full test run overlapped it). It took 15034 ms against the 15 s limit. The message is only Vitest's stack marker STACK_TRACE_ERROR, which is how the JSON report showed the timeout. Alone it passes in about 4 to 5 s with the same seed. The product is not at fault.
what_should_happen: A test of one regular expression does not depend on how long a heavy import takes on a busy machine.
repro: Only on a busy machine: TZ=Asia/Kolkata npx vitest run --sequence.shuffle --sequence.seed=1999893004. Alone it passes: npx vitest run src/lib/assistant/__tests__/decide.test.ts --sequence.shuffle --sequence.seed=1999893004
root_cause_guess: src/lib/assistant/__tests__/decide.test.ts:107 imports @/lib/assistant/pipeline inside the test, so the import counts against testTimeout (vitest.config.ts:9). The test uses only the CONTACT regular expression. Likely cause, from the timing; not reproduced on purpose, so as not to load a shared machine.
class: timing: import cost counted against the test's limit

title: 'a long sentence resolves inside 20 ms at p95' fails when the machine is busy
what_happens: Failed in 3 of 20 runs (14, 18, 19), with a p95 of 27.6 ms in the first failure. Alone, with the same three seeds, it passes, and the whole test takes 131 to 263 ms for its 60 tries. This does not show a slow resolver. OPEN-15, a test with the same kind of clock limit, did not fail in these 20 runs.
what_should_happen: A speed limit is measured where nothing else competes for the CPU, not inside a full parallel test run.
repro: Only on a busy machine: TZ=Asia/Kolkata npx vitest run --sequence.shuffle --sequence.seed=1833234340. Alone it passes: npx vitest run src/lib/thunai/briefturn.test.ts --sequence.shuffle --sequence.seed=1833234340
root_cause_guess: src/lib/thunai/briefturn.test.ts:102 checks wall-clock time over 60 samples, so 3 slow samples are enough to fail. Likely cause: CPU contention from the other test files and agents. Not reproduced on purpose, so as not to load a shared machine.
class: timing: wall-clock limit inside a parallel run
